mainTopic: Whether רבי יוסי argues in the first משנה of the פרק; then the new משנה about money owed to one of two people, and when a doubt makes someone pay both claimants.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a question about רבי יוסי. רב יהודה and רבי אלעזר say רבי יוסי argues even in the first משנה of the פרק and that the הלכה follows him there. רבי יוחנן says רבי יוסי agrees there, because the שומר already said 'I will pay.' Then a new משנה begins. A person who admits he robbed one of two people, or holds a deposit from the father of one of them, must pay each of them a full מנה. When two depositors both claim the larger amount, each gets what is surely his, and the rest is set aside until אליהו comes. רבי יוסי says the whole amount is set aside, so the liar loses too. The גמרא resolves the contradictions between these rulings in three ways: a robber is fined for his sin, a שומר pays both only if he should have kept track, and a robber who comes forward on his own to clear himself before Heaven pays everyone. Finally the גמרא asks what the robber says when he is sued. רב יהודה reports that רב said he stays silent, and רב מתנה's different report continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Is the halacha like רבי יוסי even in the first case?
steps.stepSummary: The end of a question: assuming רבי יוסי argues even in the first משנה of the פרק, is the הלכה like him there too?
steps.simpleTranslation: [Was רבי יוסי arguing] even in the first משנה? Is the הלכה like him or not like him?
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining in the middle of a question that began on the previous page. Someone is asking whether רבי יוסי's opinion also applies to the first משנה of the פרק, and if so, whether we rule like him there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first משנה of the פרק is about a שומר who paid for a lost deposit instead of swearing. If רבי יוסי argues there, he would hold that even in that case the thief's double payment (כפל) goes to the owner. The question has two parts: does רבי יוסי really argue there, and if so, do we follow him?

keyTerms.meaning: In the first case, meaning the first משנה of this פרק
The practical law follows his opinion
The practical law does not follow his opinion

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not the start of the question. The words before it, asking if רבי יוסי argued 'even in the first case,' are on the previous page.

phrases.english: even in the first [case],
phrases.notes: This continues the question from the previous page: was רבי יוסי arguing even in the first משנה of the פרק?

phrases.english: is the halacha like him
or is the halacha not like him?

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲלָכָה כְּמוֹתוֹ אוֹ אֵין הֲלָכָה כְּמוֹתוֹ
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי יוסי argues even in the first משנה of the פרק, and whether the הלכה follows him there.

steps.title: Yes, he argues there, and the halacha is like him
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה answers that רבי יוסי argues even in the first משנה, and the הלכה is like him even there.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: רבי יוסי argued even in the first case, and the הלכה is like him even in the first case.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers both parts of the question. Yes, רבי יוסי argues in the first משנה too, and yes, we rule like him there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer goes beyond the minimum. It does not only say what רבי יוסי thinks; it also sets the practical law for the first משנה like רבי יוסי.

keyTerms.meaning: He said to him
He was in disagreement, he argued

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: חָלוּק הָיָה רַבִּי יוֹסֵי
phrases.english: He said to him: Rabbi Yosei disagreed
phrases.notes: The one answering is רב יהודה.

phrases.english: even in the first [case],
and the halacha is like him even in the first [case].

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: חָלוּק הָיָה רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אַף בָּרִאשׁוֹנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יוסי argues even in the first משנה, and the הלכה follows him there.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר says the same thing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings support: רבי אלעזר also said that רבי יוסי argues in the first משנה and the הלכה is like him.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also said: רבי אלעזר said: רבי יוסי argued even in the first case, and the הלכה is like him even in the first case.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that רב יהודה's answer was also said by another אמורא, רבי אלעזר, in the same words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'אתמר נמי' means this was also stated elsewhere, so it backs up the answer of step 2. But it also sets up a dispute, because רבי יוחנן is about to disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also stated, a supporting quote from another אמורא
An אמורא of ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: It was also stated.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: חָלוּק הָיָה רַבִּי יוֹסֵי
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said: Rabbi Yosei disagreed
even in the first [case],
and the halacha is like him even in the first [case].

steps.triggerLanguage: אִתְּמַר נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 2 with the same statement from רבי אלעזר.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The identical statement of רבי אלעזר.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: רבי יוסי agreed in the first case
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן disagrees: רבי יוסי agrees in the first משנה, because the שומר had already paid.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: רבי יוסי agreed in the first case, because he had already paid.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives the opposite view. In the first משנה, רבי יוסי does not argue, because there the שומר had already paid the owner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By paying, the שומר earned the rights to the animal, so even רבי יוסי agrees the double payment goes to him. So for רבי יוחנן there is no argument in the first משנה at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Agrees, admits the other view in this case
Because he already paid

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
Rabbi Yosei agreed in the first [case]
because he had already paid.
phrases.notes: 'He' is the שומר, who paid the owner for the deposit.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: מוֹדֶה הָיָה רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בָּרִאשׁוֹנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי אלעזר in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי agrees in the first משנה that the כפל goes to the שומר, because the שומר already paid.

steps.title: But רבי יוחנן said paying is not needed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: רבי יוחנן's wording implies actual payment is needed, but elsewhere he said saying 'I will pay' is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he paid, yes; if he did not pay, no? But רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: 'paid' does not mean actually paid; rather, once he said 'I will pay,' even if he has not paid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a contradiction between two statements of רבי יוחנן. One sounds like actual payment is needed, the other says just committing to pay is enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: From 'because he already paid' we would learn that without paying, the שומר does not get the double payment. But רבי יוחנן himself explained the משנה's word 'paid' as meaning 'said I will pay.' So which is it?

keyTerms.meaning: Yes
But didn't he say? Introduces a contradicting source
Actually, literally
I hereby will pay

phrases.english: [If] he paid, yes; [if] he did not pay, no?
But didn't Rabbi Chiya bar Abba say
[that] Rabbi Yochanan said:
"Paid" does not mean actually paid,
phrases.notes: He is explaining the word 'שילם' in the first משנה of the פרק.

phrases.english: rather, once he said "I will pay,"
even though he did not [yet] pay.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of רבי יוחנן's statement in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'שכבר שילם' in רבי יוחנן's statement.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It implies actual payment is required, but רבי יוחנן elsewhere says a commitment to pay is enough.

steps.title: Fix the wording: he already said I will pay
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers by changing the wording: רבי יוסי agreed because the שומר already said 'I will pay.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: רבי יוסי agreed in the first case, because he had already said 'I will pay.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the contradiction by rewording רבי יוחנן's statement. It was never about actual payment, only about saying 'I will pay.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now both statements of רבי יוחנן match. What makes רבי יוסי agree is the שומר's commitment to pay, not handing over the money.

keyTerms.meaning: Say instead, read the statement this way

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יוחנן, רבי יוסי agrees in the first משנה because the שומר committed to pay ('הריני משלם'), even before he actually paid. רב יהודה and רבי אלעזר say רבי יוסי argues there and the הלכה is like him.

phrases.aramaic: אֵימָא: מוֹדֶה הָיָה רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בָּרִאשׁוֹנָה
phrases.english: Say: Rabbi Yosei agreed in the first [case]
because he had already said "I will pay."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָא: מוֹדֶה הָיָה רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בָּרִאשׁוֹנָה שֶׁכְּבָר אָמַר ״הֲרֵינִי מְשַׁלֵּם״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 5.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוחנן meant the commitment 'הריני משלם' is enough.

steps.title: New משנה: owing one of two people
steps.stepSummary: A person admits he robbed one of two people, or holds a deposit from the father of one of them, but does not know which; he must pay each one a מנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If he said to two people: I robbed one of you of a מנה and I don't know which of you; or: the father of one of you deposited a מנה with me and I don't know which one, he gives this one a מנה and that one a מנה, because he admitted on his own.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. Someone knows he owes a מנה to one of two people but does not know which, and he must pay both of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He pays double so that the real owner surely gets his money back. The reason given is that he admitted by himself; nobody sued him, so he must do whatever it takes to fully return what he owes.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מתניתין, our משנה
I robbed
A sum of one hundred דינרים
Deposited for safekeeping
Because he admitted on his own

steps.confusionAlert: He does not split one מנה between them. Each one gets a full מנה, so he pays two hundred in total.

phrases.english: MISHNAH: [If] he said to two people:
I robbed one of you of a maneh
and I don't know which of you.
Or: the father of one of you
deposited a maneh with me
and I don't know which one he is –
he gives this one a maneh and that one a maneh,
because he admitted on his own.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ אָמַר לִשְׁנַיִם: גָּזַלְתִּי לְאֶחָד מִכֶּם מָנֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new משנה and a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who admits on his own that he owes a מנה to one of two people, without knowing which, must pay each of them a full מנה.

steps.title: Two deposits of 100 and 200, and both claim 200
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that each depositor gets a מנה, and the disputed מנה is set aside until אליהו comes.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two people left money with one person: one left 100 and the other left 200. Each one says, 'Mine was the 200.' The שומר gives each of them 100, and the rest stays put away until אליהו comes.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a new case: two people left different amounts with one שומר, and both claim the bigger amount. The ruling is that each gets the 100 that is surely his, and the extra 100 waits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees each depositor left at least a מנה, so each can safely get one מנה. The only question is the extra מנה, and since we cannot know who is telling the truth, it is set aside until אליהו comes and tells us.

keyTerms.meaning: they deposited, left something with someone for safekeeping
a coin amount equal to 100 דינרים
two hundred (דינרים)
it will stay put away, untouched
until אליהו comes, meaning until someone can tell us the truth

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the extra 100 goes back to the שומר or is split. It stays put away, belonging to nobody for now, until the truth comes out.

phrases.english: Two people who deposited with one person,
this one 100 and that one 200.
This one says: Mine was 200,
and that one says: Mine was 200.
He gives this one 100 and that one 100,
and the rest will stay put away
until אליהו comes.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁנַיִם שֶׁהִפְקִידוּ אֵצֶל אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new case in the משנה, after the case of the person who robbed one of two people.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each claimant gets the amount that surely belongs to him (a מנה), and the disputed amount is set aside until אליהו comes.

steps.title: רבי יוסי says everything should be set aside
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי argues: if each gets a מנה, the liar loses nothing, so the whole deposit should be set aside.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said: If so, what did the cheater lose? Instead, all of the money should stay put away until אליהו comes.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי disagrees with the ruling we just learned. He says the whole amount, not just the extra מנה, should be set aside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the first view, the liar risks nothing: at worst he gets back his own מנה. רבי יוסי wants the liar to stand to lose his own money too. That gives him a reason to admit the truth.

keyTerms.meaning: lost
the cheater, the one lying
everything, the whole amount

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows two ways to handle doubt: give each person what is surely his, or hold everything back so the liar has a reason to admit the truth.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said:
If so, what did the cheater lose?
Rather, everything will stay put away
until אליהו comes.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: אִם כֵּן, מָה הִפְסִיד הָרַמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A disagreeing opinion on the ruling of step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The whole deposit is set aside until אליהו comes, so the liar loses too.

steps.title: The same case with two vessels of different value
steps.stepSummary: With two vessels worth 100 and 1,000, one person gets the small vessel, the other gets the small vessel's value from the big one, and the rest is set aside.
steps.simpleTranslation: The same goes for two vessels, one worth 100 and one worth 1,000 זוז. Each says, 'The nice one is mine.' The שומר gives the small vessel to one of them. From the big vessel he gives the other the value of the small one, and the rest stays put away until אליהו comes.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה repeats the same idea, but now with objects instead of money. Each person gets something worth the small vessel, and the extra value waits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An object cannot be split like coins. So one person takes the small vessel. The big vessel is used to pay the other person the small vessel's value. Whatever value is left over is set aside, just like the extra מנה in step 8.

keyTerms.meaning: vessels, objects
worth; also 'the nice (expensive) one'
a silver coin, the same as a דינר
the value of the small vessel

phrases.english: And likewise, two vessels,
one worth 100,
and one worth 1,000 זוז,
this one says: The expensive one is mine,
and that one says: The expensive one is mine –
he gives the small one to one of them,
and from out of the big one
phrases.notes: He means from the big vessel's value, since a vessel cannot be cut in pieces.

phrases.english: he gives the value of the small one to the other,
and the rest will stay put away
until אליהו comes.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן שְׁנֵי כֵלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the ruling of step 8 to vessels instead of money.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each gets the value of the small vessel, and the extra value of the big vessel is set aside.

steps.title: רבי יוסי repeats his view for the vessels
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי again says the cheater would lose nothing, so both vessels should be set aside.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said: If so, what did the cheater lose? Instead, everything should stay put away until אליהו comes.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי gives the same objection for the vessels case. Both vessels should be put away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His reasoning is exactly the same as in step 9. The משנה repeats it to show that he holds this way for objects too, not only for money.
steps.whatToRemember: In both cases, the תנא קמא gives each person what is surely his and sets aside only the disputed part. רבי יוסי sets aside everything so that the liar loses as well.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said:
If so, what did the cheater lose?
Rather, everything will stay put away
until אליהו comes.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: אִם כֵּן מָה הִפְסִיד הָרַמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The same disagreement as step 9, now applied to the vessels case in step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both vessels are set aside until אליהו comes.

steps.title: The גמרא learns that in doubt we take money away from where it is
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers from the משנה that in a case of doubt we take money out of the holder's hands and do not leave it in place.
steps.simpleTranslation: It seems that in a case of doubt we take money out of someone's hands. We do not say, 'Leave the money with its owner.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens its discussion with a conclusion it draws from the משנה. This sets up the questions that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first case of the משנה, the man who does not know whom he robbed must pay a full מנה to each of the two people, even though only one of them is really owed. That suggests we take money out of someone's hands because of a doubt. Normally the rule is to leave money with whoever holds it, so this inference is surprising, and the גמרא will need to deal with it.

keyTerms.meaning: it seems, we see from here
because of a doubt
we take money out (of someone's hands)
leave the money with the one who holds it now

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the final halacha. It is a conclusion the גמרא draws from the משנה, and the גמרא will go on to discuss it.
steps.whyThisMatters: אוקי ממונא בחזקת מריה is a basic rule in money cases. So a משנה that seems to go against it needs to be explained.

phrases.english: GEMARA: It seems that because of a doubt
we take money out of someone's hands,
and we do not say:
Leave the money in the possession of its owner.
phrases.notes: "Its owner" here means whoever is holding the money right now.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלְמָא מִסְּפֵיקָא מַפְּקִינַן מָמוֹנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא begins its discussion of the משנה by drawing a general rule from it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From the משנה it seems that money is taken away from its holder because of a doubt, instead of being left in place.

steps.title: A contradiction from the two-depositors case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the case of two depositors, where the disputed money is set aside, to challenge the robbery case, where both claimants are paid.
steps.simpleTranslation: And raise a contradiction: Two people deposited money with one person. One gave a מנה and the other gave two hundred. Each one says, "The two hundred is mine." The שומר gives each of them a מנה, and the rest is set aside until אליהו comes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges what it just learned in step 12. In the robbery case the person pays both claimants, but in this deposit case the disputed money is not paid out to either one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 12 the גמרא learned that when there is a doubt, the money is taken out of the holder's hands and both sides are paid. Here, in the two-depositors case, the disputed מנה stays set aside and nobody gets it. So the two rulings seem to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: And raise a contradiction. Another source is brought that seems to clash with the first.
They deposited, meaning they gave money to someone to watch.
A sum of one hundred דינרים.
Until אליהו comes. The money stays put with nobody using it.

steps.confusionAlert: This is the same משנה case from step 8. The גמרא is quoting it again here for a new reason: to use it as a challenge.

phrases.english: And raise a contradiction:
phrases.notes: The challenge is against the robbery ruling from step 12, where both people get paid.

phrases.english: Two people who deposited with one person,
this one a מנה and that one two hundred,
this one says, "Mine was two hundred,"
and that one says, "Mine was two hundred" –
he gives this one a מנה and that one a מנה,
and the rest will be set aside
until אליהו comes.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּרְמִינְהִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the inference of step 12 by using the deposit case.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that in a doubt the money is taken out of the holder's hands and both claimants are paid.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the deposit case the doubtful money is not paid to both sides. It is set aside instead.

steps.title: A robber is fined, a שומר is not
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that a robber sinned, so the רבנן fined him by making him pay both. A שומר did nothing wrong, so he is not fined.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Are you comparing a deposit to a robbery? A robber did something forbidden, so the רבנן fined him. A שומר who holds a deposit did nothing forbidden, so the רבנן did not fine him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction by showing that the two cases are not alike.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Paying both claimants in the robbery case is a קנס, a fine, because the robber committed an איסור. A שומר never sinned, so there is no reason to fine him. He only has to give out what is clearly owed.

keyTerms.meaning: A deposit, meaning money or an item given to someone to watch.
Robbery.
Something forbidden. Here it means an איסור that was done.
The רבנן fined him.

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that paying both sides in the robbery case is a penalty. It is not the basic rule for every case of doubt.

phrases.english: He said to him:
Are you comparing a deposit to a robbery?
In robbery, where he did something forbidden –
the רבנן fined him,
in a deposit, where he did nothing forbidden –
the רבנן did not fine him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: פִּקָּדוֹן אַגָּזֵל קָא רָמֵית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: a fine applies to a sinner but not to an innocent שומר.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Robbery and deposit cases of doubt should follow the same rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: A robber pays both claimants as a קנס. A שומר, who did nothing wrong, is not fined.

steps.title: Two deposit cases that seem to clash
steps.stepSummary: Even within deposit cases there is a contradiction. In the first case of the משנה the שומר pays both claimants, but in the two-depositors case he does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they set deposit against deposit, and robbery against robbery. Deposit against deposit: the first part of the משנה teaches, "Or the father of one of you deposited a מנה with me, and I don't know which one," and he gives each one a מנה. Yet raise a contradiction: two people who deposited, and so on, where the disputed money is set aside!
steps.whatsHappening: The answer in step 14 does not settle everything. The גמרא now shows that two deposit cases, where there is no sin and no fine, still get different rulings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the רישא, a שומר who does not know whose father gave him a מנה pays a full מנה to each person. In the two-depositors case, he does not pay out the disputed מנה at all. The "robbery versus deposit" answer cannot explain this, because both cases here are deposits.

keyTerms.meaning: The first part of a משנה or ברייתא.
The father of one of you.
And so on. The rest of the quote is known.

phrases.english: And they set deposit against deposit,
and robbery against robbery.
phrases.notes: The גמרא names both contradictions here. It explains the deposit one first, and the robbery one comes in step 17.

phrases.english: Deposit against deposit:
as the first part teaches:
"Or the father of one of you
deposited a מנה with me,
and I don't know which one it is,"
he gives this one a מנה and that one a מנה.
Yet raise a contradiction: "Two who deposited," and so on!
phrases.notes: This is the case from step 13, where the disputed money is set aside until אליהו comes.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּרְמִי פִּקָּדוֹן אַפִּקָּדוֹן, וּרְמִי גָּזֵל אַגָּזֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a harder contradiction that the answer of step 14 cannot solve.
steps.kashyaTarget: The deposit rulings of the משנה: the רישא, where both are paid, against the סיפא, where the money is set aside.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both cases are deposits with no sin involved, yet one pays both claimants and the other does not.

steps.title: רבא: should the שומר have kept track?
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains the difference. In the first case the שומר should have kept track of who gave what, so he pays both. In the second case both people deposited together and did not watch each other, so he did not need to keep track.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: In the first case the שומר is treated like someone who was given two separate bundles, because he should have paid attention. In the later case he is treated like someone who was given one bundle, because he did not need to pay attention. This is when both deposited together at one time, so he can say to them: "You yourselves were not careful with each other. Should I be careful?"
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the deposit-against-deposit contradiction by asking whether the שומר was expected to keep track.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Where the שומר should have noted who gave him the money, forgetting is his fault, so he pays each claimant. Where the two depositors handed over their money together without minding each other, his confusion is not his fault. So he gives each one only the מנה that is certain and sets the rest aside.

keyTerms.meaning: Bundles, meaning money wrapped up in separate packets.
One bundle.
To pay close attention or keep careful track.
Together with each other.
I am careful or particular.

steps.whatToRemember: Paying both claimants comes from fault. A robber is fined for his sin, and a שומר pays both if he should have kept track. If the depositors themselves were careless with each other, the שומר pays only what is certain and the rest waits for אליהו.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a clear rule: a שומר's duty to pay both claimants depends on whether he was expected to keep track.

phrases.english: רבא said:
In the first case, he is treated like one
with whom they deposited in two bundles,
because he should have paid attention.
In the later case, he is treated like one
with whom they deposited in one bundle,
because he did not need to pay attention,
for example, where both of them deposited
together at one time,
so he can say to them:
"You yourselves were not careful with each other,
should I be careful?"

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: רֵישָׁא נַעֲשָׂה כְּמִי שֶׁהִפְקִידוּ לוֹ בִּשְׁנֵי כְרִיכוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the deposit-against-deposit contradiction from step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases by whether the שומר had a duty to keep track.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All deposit cases of doubt should be handled the same way.
steps.terutzMaskana: Where the שומר should have kept track, he pays both claimants. Where the two depositors gave together and did not watch each other, he pays only what is certain.

steps.title: Setting up a contradiction between two robbery rulings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא announces it will contrast robbery with robbery, and first quotes our משנה: someone unsure which of two people he robbed (or whose father deposited with him) pays a מנה to each.
steps.simpleTranslation: They pointed out a contradiction between one robbery case and another. Our משנה says: if a person tells two people, 'I robbed one of you of a hundred and I don't know which one,' or 'The father of one of you deposited a hundred with me and I don't know whose father,' he gives a hundred to each.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא quotes our משנה as the first side of a contradiction, and the second side comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה makes the robber pay double so that the real victim surely gets his money. The גמרא repeats this ruling here because it is about to compare it with a different robbery ruling that seems to say the opposite.

keyTerms.meaning: And they contrasted (pointed out a contradiction between two sources)
Robbery
A sum of one hundred דינרים
Deposited (gave for safekeeping)

phrases.english: And they contrasted a robbery ruling with a robbery ruling.
It is taught here:
If one said to two people:
I robbed one of you of a hundred dinars,
and I do not know which of you it was,
or: the father of one of you
deposited a hundred dinars with me,
and I do not know which one he is,
he gives this one a hundred and that one a hundred.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּרְמִי גָּזֵל אַגָּזֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling the deposit contradictions, the גמרא opens a new contradiction about robbery itself.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling of our משנה that the robber pays both claimants.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup only; the opposing source is brought in the next step.

steps.title: רבי טרפון says the robber only puts the money down between the claimants
steps.stepSummary: A משנה in יבמות rules that a man who robbed one of five people places the stolen item among them and leaves, showing that a ספק does not take money out of the holder's hands.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a different source says: if someone robbed one of five people and doesn't know which, and each one says 'He robbed me,' he puts the stolen item down among them and walks away. That is רבי טרפון's view. So it seems that because of a doubt we don't take money out of someone's hands; we leave the money with the one who holds it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the second side of the contradiction: in יבמות the robber does not pay each claimant, he only leaves one payment for them to divide.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In our משנה the robber pays everyone, but here he pays only once. The גמרא concludes that this source holds a ספק is not enough to make someone pay extra money, which clashes with our משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: And they raised a contradiction from another source
He places the stolen item between them
Because of a doubt
We do not take money out (of the holder's hands)
In the possession of its (current) owner

phrases.english: And they raised a contradiction:
phrases.notes: The source is a משנה in יבמות 118b.

phrases.english: If one robbed one of five people,
and he does not know which of them he robbed,
this one says: He robbed me,
and that one says: He robbed me,
he places the stolen item between them and withdraws,
These are the words of Rabbi Tarfon.
Apparently, because of a doubt
we do not take money out of someone's hands,
and we say:
Leave the money in the possession of its owner.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּרְמִינְהִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the opposing source for the contradiction set up in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: Our משנה's ruling that the robber pays both people.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי טרפון rules that in a ספק the robber pays only once, so a doubt does not take extra money from him, yet our משנה makes him pay everyone.

steps.title: How do we know our משנה follows רבי טרפון?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why there is a contradiction at all: maybe our משנה follows a different תנא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do we know that our משנה here follows רבי טרפון?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to check whether the contradiction is real. If our משנה is someone else's opinion, the two sources simply disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A contradiction only matters if both sources are by the same person. The גמרא wants proof that רבי טרפון himself would agree with our משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where (do we know)?
Our משנה

phrases.english: And from where do we know
that our משנה here
is the opinion of Rabbi Tarfon?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִמַּאי דְּמַתְנִיתִין דְּהָכָא רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions whether the contradiction raised in step 18 is valid.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Proof that our משנה is by רבי טרפון, so that the two sources really clash.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows רבי טרפון agrees with our משנה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא on the יבמות משנה says רבי טרפון agrees that a man who robbed one of two people pays each a מנה, which matches our משנה exactly.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it was taught about that משנה: רבי טרפון agrees that if someone says to two people, 'I robbed one of you of a hundred and I don't know which,' he gives a hundred to each.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a ברייתא shows רבי טרפון himself rules like our משנה. So now רבי טרפון seems to contradict himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This proves the contradiction is real: the same רבי טרפון says 'put it down and leave' in one case and 'pay both' in another. That is now the problem that needs answering.

keyTerms.meaning: About that (source)
Agrees (concedes)

phrases.english: Because it is taught about that משנה:
phrases.notes: This is a ברייתא that comments on the משנה in יבמות.

phrases.english: Rabbi Tarfon agrees
in a case where one says to two people:
I robbed one of you of a hundred dinars,
and I do not know which of you it was,
that he gives this one a hundred and that one a hundred.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּקָתָנֵי עֲלַהּ דְּהַהִיא מוֹדֶה רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 19 and confirms the contradiction from step 18 is real.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A ברייתא records רבי טרפון agreeing that a robber of one of two people pays both, exactly like our משנה.

steps.title: Being sued in court versus coming on his own to clear himself before Heaven
steps.stepSummary: In יבמות the claimants are demanding money from him, so he pays only once. Here he came forward on his own to fix his sin before Heaven, so he pays both.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, the people are claiming money from him. Here, he comes on his own to clear himself before Heaven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves רבי טרפון's two rulings by showing they are about different situations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When claimants sue him, the court can only make him pay what is proven, so he puts one payment down. When he wants to be right with Heaven, he must make sure the real victim gets paid, so he pays everyone. Both rulings fit רבי טרפון.

keyTerms.meaning: They are claiming from him (suing him)
To fulfill his duty to Heaven (to fully clear himself before God)

steps.confusionAlert: Paying both is not something the court forces on him here. It is what he must do if he wants to fully clear himself before Heaven.

phrases.english: There, it is where they are claiming from him,
phrases.notes: 'There' is the יבמות case of the five people.

phrases.english: here, it is where he comes to fulfill his duty to Heaven.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם דְּקָא תָבְעִי לֵיהּ, הָכָא בְּבָא לָצֵאת יְדֵי שָׁמַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction within רבי טרפון confirmed in step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (court claim vs. voluntary return to clear himself before Heaven)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי טרפון contradicts himself, once saying pay only once and once saying pay both.
steps.terutzMaskana: Under court claims he pays only once. When he comes forward to clear himself before Heaven, he pays everyone.

steps.title: The משנה's wording 'he admitted on his own' supports the answer
steps.stepSummary: Our משנה says the robber 'admitted on his own,' which fits the answer that he came forward by himself to clear himself before Heaven. The גמרא accepts this.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wording supports this too, since it says: 'because he admitted on his own.' Learn from it that this is right.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finds support for its answer in the exact words of our משנה and closes the topic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'on his own' show that nobody sued him and he came forward himself. That is exactly the 'clearing himself before Heaven' situation, so the משנה's wording supports the answer.

keyTerms.meaning: The wording is also precise (it supports this)
Because he admitted on his own
Learn from it (this is proven)

steps.whatToRemember: A robber who doesn't know whom he robbed pays only once if he is sued in court. If he comes forward on his own to clear himself before Heaven, he pays every possible victim. Both rulings are רבי טרפון's view.

phrases.english: The wording is also precise,
for it teaches: because he admitted on his own.
phrases.notes: These words are from the end of our משנה.

phrases.english: Learn from it that this is so.

steps.triggerLanguage: דַּיְקָא נָמֵי דְּקָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 21 from the wording of our משנה.
steps.raayaObject: The answer that our משנה is about someone clearing himself before Heaven.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The phrase 'שהודה מפי עצמו' in our משנה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Our משנה is about a robber who came forward on his own, so he pays both claimants. This does not contradict רבי טרפון's ruling in יבמות.

steps.title: In the demanding case, what does the robber say back?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes its earlier answer, that in יבמות the claimants are demanding money from the robber, and asks what the robber says in reply.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: There, it is a case where they are demanding money from him. And the other one, the robber, what does he claim?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the answer from step 21 so it can ask a follow-up question about it. This is setting up the next move: two reports of what רב said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 21 told us only what the claimants are doing: demanding their money. It did not tell us how the robber answers them. The גמרא wants the case fully defined, so it asks what the robber's side of the story is.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Master said'. A formula for quoting an earlier statement in order to discuss it further.
They are demanding from him, meaning the claimants are pressing him for their money.
'The other one'. Here it means the robber.
Claims or argues back in a dispute.

steps.confusionAlert: 'אמר מר' here is not a new opinion. The גמרא is simply quoting its own answer from step 21 so it can look at it more closely.

phrases.english: The Master said:
phrases.notes: This quotes the answer from step 21 about the case in יבמות.

phrases.english: There, it is where they are demanding from him.
And the other one, what does he claim?
phrases.notes: 'The other one' is the robber, who is facing the people demanding money.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: הָתָם דְּקָא תָבְעִי לֵיהּ. וְהַלָּה מָה טוֹעֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the answer from step 21 was accepted in step 22, the גמרא returns to that answer to define its case more precisely.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: In the יבמות case where the claimants demand payment, what is the robber's reply to them?

steps.title: רב יהודה in the name of רב: the robber stays silent
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה reports that רב said the robber is silent and gives no answer to the claimants.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: The other one is silent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the first answer: according to רב יהודה's report of רב, the robber says nothing when the claimants demand their money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The robber does not deny the robbery, and he also does not point to any one claimant as the person he robbed. Since he stays silent, this is the case where the ruling of יבמות applies: he places the money among them and leaves.

keyTerms.meaning: רב יהודה reports a teaching in the name of his teacher רב.
Is silent. Here the robber gives no reply.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav:
The other one is silent.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: הַלָּה שׁוֹתֵק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The robber stays silent when the claimants demand payment.

steps.title: רב מתנה begins a different report in the name of רב
steps.stepSummary: רב מתנה begins to report a different version of what רב said about the robber's reply.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מתנה said in the name of רב: The other one...
steps.whatsHappening: A second student of רב begins to give his own version of what the robber says. His sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two students are passing on רב's teaching, and they remember it differently. רב יהודה said the robber is silent, while רב מתנה is about to describe a different reply. The details of his version come on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא and a student of רב. Here he gives a second report of רב's words.
'Said in the name of רב'. Here it shows that two students are reporting the same teacher.

steps.confusionAlert: רב יהודה and רב מתנה are not giving their own personal opinions. Both are reporting what their teacher רב said, and they remember his words differently.

phrases.english: Rav Mattana said in the name of Rav:
The other one
phrases.notes: The sentence stops here. What the robber says in רב מתנה's version continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב מַתְנָה אָמַר רַב: הַלָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second report of רב's answer to the question in step 23, different from רב יהודה's report in step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A different report of the robber's reply in the name of רב. The content continues on the next amud.
